clauses.reason: Section 1 of Executive Order 11462 (34 FR 5983, signed 1969-03-28) orders all executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies, including their field services, closed on Monday, March 31, 1969, as a mark of respect for General of the Army Dwight David Eisenhower. The command is tied to that one day and ends with it by the order's own terms. The end is recorded as 1969-03-31, inclusive (the closing runs through that day); the exclusive reading is that it stops when that day begins. Actor: the order itself; the cited source is its own held text, which names the day. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

Section 2 of Executive Order 11462 provides that section 1 does not apply to those offices and installations, or parts of them, in the Department of State, the Department of Defense or other agencies which their heads determine should remain open for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons. It limits section 1 and can operate only while the closing of March 31, 1969 operates, so it ends on the same day, 1969-03-31, inclusive (exclusive reading: when that day begins). Actor: the order itself, through the day stated in section 1. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

Section 3 of Executive Order 11462 authorizes the heads of executive departments, independent establishments and other Government agencies to excuse from duty, without charge to leave, for the remainder of the tour of duty on Friday, March 28, 1969, any employee engaged in the performance of duty at the time of General Eisenhower's death at 12:25 p.m. on that day. The authority is tied to that one day and ends with it by the order's own terms. The end is recorded as 1969-03-28, inclusive (exclusive reading: when that day begins). Actor: the order itself. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

inventory_overrides.reason: The dossier inventory omitted section 1, the operative closing command, which begins with the heading of section 1 at offset 829 and ends before section 2 at offset 1151 of the held text; it is added as its own scope. Sections 2 and 3 keep their dossier offsets.
Section 2 as in the dossier inventory, offsets 1151 to 1526 of the held text; kept unchanged because every scope of the corrected inventory needs its own source span.
Section 3 as in the dossier inventory, offsets 1527 to 1891 of the held text; kept unchanged because every scope of the corrected inventory needs its own source span.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 11462 (34 FR 5983, filed April 1, 1969; the govinfo PDF text layer), headed Executive Order 11462, Providing for the closing of Government departments and agencies on March 31, 1969, and for the granting of administrative leave on March 28, 1969, signed by Richard Nixon and dated March 28, 1969; number, date and subject agree with the census register. Inventory: the dossier listed only sections 2 and 3; section 1, which orders all executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies, including their field services, closed on Monday, March 31, 1969, as a mark of respect for General of the Army Dwight David Eisenhower, was omitted. I add it as its own scope and keep sections 2 and 3: section 2 provides that section 1 does not apply to offices and installations, or parts, that their heads determine should remain open for reasons of national security or defense or other public reasons; section 3 lets the heads of departments and agencies excuse from duty, without charge to leave, for the remainder of the tour of duty on Friday, March 28, 1969, any employee engaged in the performance of duty at the time of General Eisenhower's death at 12:25 p.m. that day. Lifecycle: each command is tied to a stated calendar day and ends with that day by the order's own terms. Sections 1 and 2 end on 1969-03-31; section 3 ends on 1969-03-28. The latest first end, 1969-03-31, is the whole-order end. The end days are recorded inclusive; the exclusive reading is that each command stops when its day begins. Searches: the U.S. Code, eCFR and Office of the Federal Register disposition-note searches record no hit for this order; a held-corpus search by number returns only this order's own printings; the order is not in the table of EO 12553.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings or continuation wording. The closing on March 31, 1969 and the excusal on March 28, 1969 were completed on those days; any absence excused under section 3 was a completed act. No continuing right or duty arising from the order after 1969-03-31 is shown in held evidence.
